Command: A priest shall not profane holy things
Summary: The command: A priest shall not profane holy things (Leviticus 22:15). Priests were not to profane the holy things of Israel which they offered to the LORD, lest they bear the iniquity of trespass.
Commandment: A priest shall not profane holy things.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The New Testament replaces the whole system of holy food: all who are in Christ are a holy priesthood (1 Peter 2:5,9), and the meal that marks God's people is the Lord's Supper, not the priestly portions. The boundary itself — holy things are not common things — is fulfilled, not continued.
Purpose: Scripture's stated ground: the holy things are the LORD's, set apart for the priesthood (Leviticus 22:3-16).
Function: Priests were not to profane the holy things of Israel which they offered to the LORD — a ceremonial law aimed at the guardians themselves. Its goal was to keep the men who handled holy things from making them common, since the priests were the very ones who could profane them. The evil was careless handling by holy hands, the slow blurring of sacred and ordinary. It restrained that by laying the iniquity of trespass on the priest who profaned, so the guardians guarded themselves.
